As a result, we completely classify all portraits of $\mathbb{Q}$-rational preperiodic points for quadratic rational maps defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ with nonabelian automorphism group, showing that there are exactly $7$ such portraits, one of which is the empty portrait.
item.dc:creator: Hasan Bilgili, Mohammad Sadek

item.title: Monogenic Fields from Polynomial Compositions with Applications
item.description: arXiv:2605.00949v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A number field $K$ is called \emph{monogenic} if its ring of integers $\mathbb{Z}_K$ can be expressed as a simple ring extension $\mathbb{Z}[\alpha]$ for some $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}_K$. A monic irreducible polynomial $f(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ is said to be monogenic if one of its roots generates both the number field and its ring of integers. In this article, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions for $[\mathbb{Z}_{K_i}:\mathbb{Z}[\alpha_i]]=1$, where $K_i=\mathbb{Q}(\alpha_i)$ and $\alpha_i$ is a root of the composed polynomial $f_i(x^k+b)$ for $i=1,2$. Here, $f_1(x)=x^n+c\sum_{j=1}^{n}(ax)^{n-j}\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ and $f_2(x)=x^n+c\sum_{j=1}^{n}a^{j-1}x^{n-j}\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ are irreducible polynomials of degree $n\ge 3$. In addition, we derive asymptotic estimates for the number of monogenic polynomials in these families under natural assumptions. As an application of our main results, we construct a class of polynomials with non-square-free discriminants. We also analyze the behavior of solutions to certain related differential equations.
item.dc:creator: Anuj Jakhar, Ravi Kalwaniya, Prabhakar Yadav

item.title: Rank-Two Drinfeld Modules over Elliptic Coordinate Rings
item.description: arXiv:2606.26851v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let ${\mathbf A}$ be the affine coordinate ring of $E\setminus\{\infty\}$, where $E$ is an elliptic curve over $\mathbb F_q$ and $\infty$ is rational. We solve the rank-two case of the open problem of explicitly classifying sign-normalized Drinfeld ${\mathbf A}$-modules in generic characteristic with a fixed determinant motive; the classification for rank greater than two remains open. Outside an explicit exceptional locus, the rank-two Drinfeld modules are parametrized by the open modular curve $Y^{q+1}=\pi(X)$ with $Y\neq0$. The polynomial $\pi$ is squarefree, and the smooth projective completion of this curve has genus $q^2$. The roots of $\pi$ split into two types. Above roots of the first type, all coefficient functions extend regularly, and their extensions yield exactly the exceptional modules. Roots of the second type correspond to cusps of the modular curve; above these roots, the coefficient family has poles.
item.dc:creator: Chuangqiang Hu, Ze-Dong Huang, Chang-An Zhao

item.title: Two-point correlations of multiplicative functions with dense orbits
item.description: arXiv:2608.26814v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{T}$ be completely multiplicative functions with dense images in the complex unit circle $\mathbb{T}$. We prove that, for every non-empty open set $U \subset \mathbb{T}^2$, the set of integers $n$ such that $(f(n),g(n+1)) \in U$ has positive upper logarithmic density, unless the pair $(f,g)$ is of a special form. This result strengthens earlier theorems of Klurman and Mangerel, as well as of Charamaras, Mountakis, and Tsinas, and yields simpler proofs.
item.dc:creator: N\'{e}o Tardy

item.title: Generalized Fermat equation over number fields
item.description: arXiv:2608.28117v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and $A,B,C\in\mathcal{O}_K\setminus\{0\}$. Put $S_K=\{\mathfrak{P}:\mathfrak{P}\mid2\}$ and $S_K'=\{\mathfrak{q}:\mathfrak{q}\mid2ABC\}$. We establish two criteria for the non-existence of non-trivial solutions of $Ax^p+By^p=Cz^p$ over $K$ for sufficiently large prime exponents $p$. Both criteria use a valuation bound on the $S_K'$-unit equation at a fixed $\mathfrak{P}\in S_K$. The first excludes all non-trivial solutions in $K^3$ when $v_{\mathfrak{P}}(A)=v_{\mathfrak{P}}(B)=m$ and $v_{\mathfrak{P}}(C)=m+k$, with $k>4v_{\mathfrak{P}}(2)$. The second, under an explicit nonvanishing condition on the coefficient valuations, excludes solutions $(a,b,c)\in(K^\times)^3$ whose $\mathfrak{P}$-valuations are not all equal. In particular, it excludes non-trivial primitive integral solutions with $\mathfrak{P}\mid abc$. Neither criterion restricts the residue degree of $\mathfrak{P}$. Both criteria hold unconditionally over every totally real field; over general number fields, we assume residual modularity and Eichler--Shimura-type conjectures. The first criterion covers a new coefficient range. In particular, under the corresponding $S_K$-unit bound, $x^p+y^p=2^rz^p$ has no non-trivial solutions in $K^3$ for each fixed $r\geq5$ and sufficiently large prime $p$. This bound holds for a set of real quadratic fields of relative density $1$. For a family of imaginary quadratic fields of relative density $5/6$, we explicitly determine the $S_K$-unit solutions and verify the valuation bound for both criteria when $A,B,C\in\{\pm2^r:r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}\}$, including the same $r\geq5$ conclusion.
item.dc:creator: Satyabrat Sahoo

item.title: On the largest prime factors less than $y$ of consecutive shifted primes
item.dc:creator: Zhiyuan Yang

item.title: Bad Reduction of Genus Two Curves with complex multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2609.22544v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study genus two curves whose Jacobians have complex multiplication by a biquadratic CM field. In this setting the Jacobian decomposes as a product of two elliptic curves with complex multiplication by orders in the same imaginary quadratic field. We derive upper bounds for the primes of stable bad reduction of such curves in terms of the discriminants of the CM orders. To do so, we give an explicit description of principally polarized abelian surfaces with CM by a biquadratic field via small CM cycles on an orthogonal Shimura variety of signature (3,2). We use it to prove an arithmetic intersection formula between such CM cycles with Humbert surfaces in terms of coefficients of incoherent Eisenstein series and representation numbers of ternary positive definite quadratic forms. Finally, employing the arithmetic properties of higher Green functions, we show that primes of stable bad reduction always exist.
item.dc:creator: Jan Hendrik Bruinier, Tonghai Yang, Peng Yu

item.title: Lower Bounds for Localised Moments of Automorphic $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2609.32673v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we describe a method to obtain lower bounds for the $2k$-th moment of values of $L$-functions localised at the central point for all real $k > 0$. In particular, for the families of quadratic twists of self-dual irreducible unitary cuspidal automorphic representations of $\operatorname{GL}_D(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$ with $D\in\{2,3,4\}$, our results are new in the range $0<k<\tfrac12$ when $D\in\{2,3\}$, and new for all $k>0$ when $D=4$.
item.dc:creator: Deep Thakur

item.title: Omega bounds for the Piltz divisor problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.33820v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We improve our earlier omega bounds for the error term in the Piltz divisor problem over number fields. Our proof uses a weighted extension of a counting theorem of Balasubramanian and Ramachandra and an extension of Lamzouri's kernel to apply the long resonance method. We also discuss applications of our results to lattice points in norm-form regions, invariant sublattices, abelian covers of curves, spectral counting, and representation growth of Heisenberg groups.
item.dc:creator: Nilmoni Karak, Kamalakshya Mahatab

item.title: Long intervals of consecutive composite values of polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.10762v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $f\in\mathbb Q[t]$ be an irreducible integer-valued polynomial of positive degree with positive leading coefficient. We show that there is a constant $c_f>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large real $X$, the interval $(X/2,X]$ contains a block of at least $c_f\log X\log\log X$ consecutive integers $n$ for which $f(n)$ is composite. The exponent of $\log\log X$ does not depend on the degree of $f$. This improves a result of Ford and Gabdullin, replacing a small fixed power of $\log\log X$ by $\log\log X$. The result includes the case $f(t)=t^2+1$.
item.dc:creator: Artyom Radomskii

item.title: A Half-Constant Upper Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.17160v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let lambda(n) denote the infimum of -min_x sum_{a in A} cos(ax) over all sets A of n positive integers. While the classical Sidon-difference construction yields lambda(n) <= (1 + o(1))sqrt(n)/2, we construct sets achieving a leading constant of 1/2: lambda(n) <= (1/2)sqrt(n) + O(n^(1/4)sqrt(log n)), establishing limsup_{n->infinity} lambda(n)/sqrt(n) <= 1/2. This construction combines a two-sided Sidon square identity, a Singer difference set, a Fejer-kernel majorant, a parity-biased deletion, and an exact-cardinality probabilistic selection. We also provide an L^4 criterion and a multiplicity bound constraining any construction with a smaller leading constant. In the opposite direction, we incorporate the L^1 norm into Bedert's boundary estimate with an explicit constant, yielding two lower bounds for f_A(x) = sum_{a in A} cos(ax): (1) -min f_A >= cn^(1/4) for every n-element set A subset of [1, Cn]; and (2) (-min f_A)^3 ||f_A||_1^2 >= cn for every n-element set A subset of N. The second bound recovers the 1/5 exponent of Bedert and Shankar and improves it whenever ||f_A||_1 is small relative to -min f_A. Numerical values of the construction are reported up to |A| = 25,440.
item.dc:creator: Bryan Bu, Fayzan Khan, Hyunjun Yi, Atharv Jha, Ishaan Chandupatla, Madhav Nagpal

item.title: Mahler Method and Vanishing Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.23435v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is motivated by the recent work of Adamczewski and Faverjon [5], who established the algebraic independence of values of Mahler functions satisfying linear functional equations. While their work is a landmark result, some proofs are long and complex. The primary aim of this paper is to simplify those proofs and provide new applications. In their proofs, a vanishing theorem for polynomials, rather than power series, is sufficient. We give a proof of the vanishing theorem without using Szemer\'edi's theorem or Corvaja-Zannier's theorem. In the case of a single transformation, we present a refined vanishing theorem, which allows us to simplify the proof of algebraic independence. We also provide an elementary proof of a vanishing theorem for $q_i$-Mahler functions with various $q_i$. As an application, we prove the algebraic independence of certain continued fractions, extending previous results by Han\v{c}l, Adamczewski, and Bundschuh and V\"a\"an\"anen in which only linear independence and transcendence had been established.
item.dc:creator: Kumiko Nishioka, Taka-aki Tanaka, Yusuke Tanuma

item.title: Zero-free half-planes for Hecke $L$-functions over number fields and Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis
item.description: arXiv:2610.26835v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In [Liu26a], varying the length and moment parameters in the cubic-theta argument of [Ope26a] gave the zero-free half-plane $Re(s)>B_{\mathrm{new}}=0.874957019420098946\ldots$ for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and for Dirichlet $L$-functions, and its optimality in the specified exponent comparison system. In this paper, we extend the argument to finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over cyclotomic fields containing $\mu_{12}$ and, by class-field descent, to every pair $(K,\eta)$ whose cyclic class field has metabelian normal closure over $\mathbb Q$, including every finite-order character over every abelian number field. Then, adapting the averaged numerator estimate developed by Xu and Sang [XS26] for Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and combining it with a limiting contradiction argument, we obtain the boundary $B_\flat=0.874886647039964\ldots$, the root near $0.8749$ of $133488B^4-376596B^3+384534B^2-167541B+26231$; it is the exact infimum of the refined comparison system, unattained by finite chains starting above it. Since the analytic argument uses only $\mu_{12}\subset F$, we run it over $F=K(\zeta_{12})$ for an arbitrary number field $K$ and descend: every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over every number field is zero-free for $Re(s)>B_\flat$, giving a uniform Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis over number fields. The analytic argument uses the exceptional-theta constructions and local calculations of the preprint [Ope26b].
item.dc:creator: Baiying Liu

item.title: Complete Determination of the Gallai--van der Waerden Number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\)
item.description: arXiv:2610.30711v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper completely determines the Gallai--van der Waerden number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\) for all integers \(r\ge 3\): \[ \mathrm{GW}(3;3,3)=\mathrm{GW}(4;3,3)=9,\qquad \mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)=r\quad (r\ge 5). \]
item.dc:creator: Yuan Si

item.title: Near-quadratic sum-product estimates in fixed number fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.36930v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a fixed number field. We prove a quantitative expansion theorem for mixed sumsets $A+B$, assuming only that $A$ is covered by relatively few cosets of a multiplicative group of small finite valuation rank. The constants are independent of the generators, their heights, and their prime ideal supports. As a consequence, if $A\subset K^\times$, $|A|=N\ge 3$, and each element has nonzero valuation at at most $k$ finite places, then every $B\subset K$ with $|B|=N$ satisfies $$ \max\{|A+B|,|AA|\} \ge N^2\exp\left[-C_K\left((k+1)\log(\log N+2)+\sqrt{(k+1)\log N}\right)\right]. $$ This is $N^{2-o(1)}$ for $k=o(\log N/\log\log N)$. We also obtain a trade-off between the additive and multiplicative deficits, estimates for iterated linear sumsets, and a transfer theorem for product constructions $A=PG$ in terms of the multiplicative deficit of $P$. The proof recovers local scales from an exact sum and bounds the remaining conditional entropy by the overlap of entropy measures on fixed trees.
item.dc:creator: Kaiqiang Zhang, Yuanguo Zeng, Yuyu Wang

item.title: Diamonds: Homology and the Central Series of Groups
item.description: arXiv:2310.08283v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish an analog of a theorem of Stallings which asserts the homomorphisms between the universal nilpotent quotients induced by a homomorphism $G \to H$ of groups are isomorphisms provided a pair of homological conditions are satisfied. Our analogy does not have a homomorphism between $G$ and $H$ but instead $G,H \leq G_0$ that satisfies a similar homological condition. We derive a few applications of this result. First, we show that there exist pairs of non-isomorphic number fields whose absolute Galois groups have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. We show that there exists pairs of non-isometric hyperbolic $n$-manifolds whose fundamental groups are residually nilpotent and have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. These are the first examples of residually nilpotent Kleinian groups with arbitrarily large nilpotent genus. Complex hyperbolic 2-manifold examples are given as well. Considering Riemann surfaces and complex hyperbolic 2-manifolds as projective curves and surfaces defined over a number field, we show the (outer) action of the absolute Galois group of the field of definition on the universal nilpotent quotients of the geometric fundamental groups are equivalent. This is in contrast to fact that the (outer) Galois action on the geometric fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve determines the curve by work of Mochizuki. In particular, the nilpotent representation theory of the geometric fundamental group is not anabelian.
item.dc:creator: Milana Golich, D. B. McReynolds

item.title: Fourier-Mukai partners of abelian varieties and K3 surfaces in positive and mixed characteristics
item.description: arXiv:2410.14065v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Fourier-Mukai equivalences of (families of) abelian varieties and K3 surfaces in positive and mixed characteristics. We first prove in any characteristics that Fourier-Mukai partners of abelian varieties are again abelian varieties. We subsequently focus on the canonical lifts of ordinary abelian varieties and ordinary K3 surfaces. For such schemes, we show that Fourier-Mukai equivalences on the special fibers can be lifted to the canonical lifts. We also prove that the relative Fourier-Mukai partners of the canonical lifts are in bijection with the Fourier-Mukai partners of the special fibers. We conclude by demonstrating that the last result can be used to recover the ordinary case of a result originally proved by Honigs, Lombardi and Tirabassi.
item.dc:creator: Riku Kurama

item.title: A note on $\mathscr{B}$-free sets and the existence of natural density
item.description: arXiv:2506.10218v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given $\mathscr{B}\subseteq\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{M}_\mathscr{B}$ be its set of multiples; $\mathscr{B}$ is called Besicovitch if $\mathcal{M}_\mathscr{B}$ has natural density. With $\mathscr{B}$ one associates its tautification $\mathscr{B}'$, the unique taut set with the same Mirsky measure, and the minimal set $\mathscr{B}^*$, which determines the unique minimal subsystem of the $\mathscr{B}$-free subshift. It is known that if $\mathscr{B}'$ is Besicovitch, then so is $\mathscr{B}$. We show that this is the only restriction: all six combinations of the Besicovitch property for $\mathscr{B},\mathscr{B}',\mathscr{B}^*$ compatible with it occur. To this end we prove that every taut set is the tautification of a Besicovitch set, and that every minimal set is the minimal set associated with a Besicovitch taut set. We also show that $\mathcal{M}_{\mathscr{B}'}\setminus\mathcal{M}_\mathscr{B}$ may have positive upper Banach density even if $\mathscr{B}$ and $\mathscr{B}'$ are both Besicovitch in which case this set has zero natural density.
item.dc:creator: Aurelia Dymek, Stanis{\l}aw Kasjan, Joanna Ku{\l}aga-Przymus

item.title: Extreme value theorem for geodesic flow on the quotient of the theta group
item.description: arXiv:2603.07649v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish an extreme value theorem for the geodesic flow $g_t$ on the hyperbolic surface $\Theta\backslash\mathbb{H}^2$ associated with the theta group $\Theta$. To capture excursions into both cusps of this surface, we introduce a generalized continued fraction algorithm obtained by splicing the even and odd--odd continued fraction maps into a single dynamical system. We prove that the natural extension of this map is isomorphic to the first return map of the geodesic flow on a suitable cross-section. Using spectral properties of the associated transfer operator, we derive a Galambos-type extreme value law for the digits of the spliced continued fraction. This symbolic result is then translated into a geometric extreme value theorem describing maximal cusp excursions of geodesics on $\Theta\backslash\mathbb{H}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Jaelin Kim, Seul Bee Lee, Seonhee Lim

item.title: The geometry of solutions to the general sextic
item.description: arXiv:2609.30422v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the geometry of the three simplest known formulas for roots of a general sextic polynomial. In contrast with work of Green on the quintic, we show that no "simultaneous uniformization" of the normal forms associated to the solutions exists. This demonstrates an intrinsic qualitative complexity of sextic equations that is not present in quintic equations. Additionally, we give a formula for the roots of a general sextic in terms of Hilbert modular cusp forms and the uniformizing differential equation of the associated Hilbert modular surface.
